1.explanation:
• NumberInput.js: core logic must read the new readOnly prop, forward it to the native <input>, disable the buttons, and add a .bx--number__input--readonly modifier class.
• __tests__/NumberInput-test.js: unit tests need new RTL assertions that the readOnly attribute is present on the <input> and that increment/decrement buttons are disabled.
• NumberInput.stories.js: the storybook needs a read-only story and a control knob for the prop for easy playground use and copy/paste.
• index.js: export the new readOnly prop in the component’s propTypes and defaultProps.
• NumberInput.mdx & docs/overview.mdx: documentation must list readOnly in the Component API, show the read-only variant in the live demo.
• e2e/components/NumberInput-test.e2e.js: end-to-end tests need a scenario that renders NumberInput with readOnly and asserts no user edits or button clicks.
• _number-input.scss in carbon-components: styling rules (transparent background, secondary text color, disabled icon colors, pointer-events none on buttons) must be added under a .bx--number__input--readonly selector to match the design tokens shown in the bug images.
1.bug_scenario: When you pass the new readOnly prop to the React NumberInput (e.g. <NumberInput readOnly />), it does not render the input element or control buttons in a read-only style or disable user edits. The designs show a special transparent fill, secondary text color, disabled icons, and no hover/focus styles on the up/down buttons. Currently the component ignores readOnly entirely, so the input remains fully editable and the increment/decrement buttons are active. The images demonstrate the intended structure, spacing, colors, and typography for the read-only state.

2. NumberInput.stories.js: must add a `readOnly` control knob and include a default story showcasing the read-only state for copy/paste.  
3. NumberInput.mdx: update the component documentation to list `readOnly` in the API table with its description.  
4. docs/overview.mdx: add a read-only variant in the live demo so maintainers can preview the state.  
5. __tests__/NumberInput-test.js: add a RTL (React Testing Library) test asserting that when `readOnly` is passed, the input has the `readonly` attribute and the appropriate CSS class applied.  
6. _number-input.scss: add new style rules targeting `input[readonly]` or the read-only modifier class to change background, text color, border, and disable pointer-events on the buttons, matching the design tokens shown in the screenshots.
2.bug_scenario:
The design images outline the desired "read-only" state for the NumberInput component: when the `readOnly` prop is set, the input field should have a distinct background, placeholder and text colors, a subtle border, and the increment/decrement buttons should be disabled (styled as disabled icons). Currently, passing `readOnly` to NumberInput has no visual or functional effect—the field still appears editable and the buttons remain active.

Key points from the images:
- Spacing and sizing remain the same as the enabled component.
- The input background switches to a light gray and the text color changes to secondary/placeholder variables.
- The border should use `$border-subtle-01` or `$border-strong-01` as shown.
- The increment/decrement icons use the disabled icon color and are non-interactive.
- Helper text and label should use the `$text-helper` and `$text-secondary` colors for the read-only state.
